answer: Each agent must keep a private sequential memory-hard crystal lattice continuously updated and must anchor it to its own non-transferable dune of prior peer seals. An attacker spawning N clones pays super-linear cost: every identity recomputes and stores a full exclusive crystal working set while it must anchor to a unique dune that cannot be pooled or shared, and failed anchor attempts burn local sequential compute that scales with dune length rather than wall-clock time.
